value.rationale: Identifying hidden multi-timescale active-force relaxation rates from macroscopic net-current noise is a motivated quantitative inverse-transport problem. The 2N+1 sample theorem gives the exact sufficient and necessary observation count when the background Brownian diffusivity is unknown and provides a sharp model-consistency test. The arbitrary-Gaussian part distinguishes global identifiability, finite-data nonidentifiability and spectral instability in this physical observable; this is useful for designing active-matter noise spectroscopy beyond routine parameter-fitting.
